## Decision

<a id="PullRequestsOnGitHub"></a>

### How a pull request is checked on GitHub

`PullRequestsOnGitHub` · `src/sdlc.ts:95`

At each pull request into main, on GitHub's Ubuntu 24.04 machine with Node.js 22: its job, named std, is a check the repository requires; it keeps GitHub from merging a pull request that changes what people decided (a trame.lock of the repository), which a person then merges (D1).

| Case | Value |
|---|---|
| on | { pullRequests: main } |
| job | std |
| runsOn | ubuntu-24.04 |
| node | 22 |
| artefacts | { days: 30 } |
| pullRequest | { review: false, merge: onceItHoldsUnlessDecided } |

- Decided by: trame
- Rejected: Only when a pull request touches the project, GitHub keeps a pull request waiting for a check it requires and that never ran; Merged by GitHub whatever it changes, what people decided would reach main without a person
- Sets the writer of: [The pull requests' workflow](#PullRequestWorkflow)

## Policy

<a id="VersionMode"></a>

### How a version is made

`VersionMode` · `src/sdlc.ts:77`

The way the standard library releases a version: its functions verified (a gap is an error), the requirements of its goals held, its decisions applied, its rules held, its packages safe, its callers identified, its data reviewed; and the foundations, as always.

And, as every policy, the foundations: no literal in a body, and a sound graph (nothing undecided, no error of the graph).

- Owner: trame
- Its obligations: [Its functions verified](#FunctionsVerified), [Its requirements held](#RequirementsServed), [Its decisions applied](#DecisionsApplied), [Its rules held](#RulesHeld), [Its packages safe](#PackagesSafe), [Its callers identified](#CallersIdentified), [Its data reviewed](#DataReviewed)
- Followed by: [The next version](#NextVersion)
